lastCompletedStory.title: WARNING: Criterion #2, anti-mock clause 2 (real I/O at each wire boundary): every test in test/setup-config-log.test.ts spawns snippets under bash, never real /bin/sh via tmux

openQuestions: CAM-513 (flaky-test-isolation, filed on main from US-R1-003) remains open and unrelated to this story's diff.
US-R2-005 (site 4 has no stale-sibling pruning, unlike sites 1/2/3/5) remains open and untouched by this story.
nextStoryContext: US-R2-004 closed the reviewer's WARNING that every prior test for buildConfigLogCapCommand (test/setup-config-log.test.ts) spawns the generated snippet directly under an explicit `bash` and never crosses the real tmux boundary the snippet is actually embedded through in production: buildSetupMenuScript's v|V case arm wraps the cap command in single quotes inside an OUTER double-quoted `tmux split-window` argument, and that whole composed line is later handed by tmux's `pipe-pane -o` to a fresh /bin/sh at runtime. Added test/integration/setup-menu-viewer-live.test.ts, a real-tmux end-to-end integration test (private -L socket per test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts's convention) that composes buildSetupMenuScript()'s actual output, spawns it in a real tmux session, presses a real 'v' keystroke (no Enter, matching the script's `read -rsn1` raw-keystroke read), and drives two ~489KB write bursts through a real config pane, each comfortably past the real 200_000-byte CONFIG_LOG_CEILING_BYTES so several real rotates fire. Writing this test caught two real production defects, both invisible to all 11 prior bash-spawn tests and both fixed by this story: (1) bash's `read -rsn1 -t 2 key` leaves `key` at its PREVIOUS value on a timeout with no new input instead of clearing it, so a single 'v' keypress re-triggered the v|V arm on every subsequent 2s poll forever, flooding the window with new viewer splits until tmux ran out of space -- fixed with an explicit `key=""` reset immediately before every timed `read` in the while-loop body; (2) bash performs command substitution ($(...)) inside double-quoted strings unconditionally regardless of any literal single-quote characters embedded in that string (confirmed against the current GNU bash manual via WebSearch, Step 5.5: backslash retains its special escaping meaning only before $, `, ", \, or newline), so buildConfigLogCapCommand's `$(wc -c < LOG)` ceiling check was being evaluated ONE TIME, EAGERLY, by the menu script's own double-quoted split-window argument at v-keypress time (typically against a byte count of 0, since the log file is freshly pre-created empty per US-R2-002), baking a permanently-frozen numeric literal into the generated command and silently disabling the entire byte-ceiling mechanism for that pipe's whole live session -- confirmed via `ps -eo command` on the real spawned pipe-pane consumer process showing the frozen literal in its argv (e.g. `test        0 -gt 1000` instead of the source's `test $(wc -c < LOG) -gt 1000`). Fixed with a new `deferCommandSubstitution(snippet)` helper (src/commands/setup.ts) that escapes every literal `$(` in the cap command's return value to `\$(` before it is interpolated into the double-quoted split-window argument, so bash's double-quote parser treats that `$` as a literal character and the substitution text survives menu-script-time evaluation unevaluated, reaching the real later-spawned pipe-pane consumer shell intact where it IS re-run on every loop iteration as originally intended; the pre-existing `${CAM_CONFIG_LOG}`/`${CAM_CONFIG_PANE}` parameter expansions in the same argument are deliberately left un-escaped since those must resolve eagerly at menu-script time to bake in the real absolute log path and pane id. The new test asserts: log size stays under 210_000 bytes after each ~489KB burst (falsifies defect 2, which without the fix leaves the log fully unbounded), exactly 3 panes exist throughout both bursts (falsifies defect 1, which without the fix would spawn extra viewer splits across the several 2s poll cycles each burst spans), the viewer's on-screen capture advances to the newest mark after each burst (falsifies the US-R2-003 freeze under a genuinely live, tmux-driven rotate rather than a direct-bash-spawned one), and the viewer pane is still command=tail (alive, not dead) at the end. Full bun test 6105 pass / 0 fail (+1 from the new test), typecheck 0 errors, full bun run check:all spine green after one justified gate resolution: file-size-budget.json raised for src/commands/setup.ts (1076->1141, the new deferCommandSubstitution helper plus its doc comment and the key="" reset), dated note prepended to _ref naming this story/CAM-510 and staged in the same commit. No knip/jscpd/coverage changes needed; no vendor/templates changes, no embed-vendor needed. Step 5.5 confirmed the bash double-quote escape rule (backslash special only before $, `, ", \, newline) via WebSearch against the current GNU Bash Reference Manual content -- aligned with and fully explains the deferCommandSubstitution fix, no correction needed. scripts/cam/prd.json was left untouched/uncommitted by this story, per the AGENT.md rule that the implementer never edits prd.json.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed the double-quote escape rule underlying deferCommandSubstitution: inside double quotes, backslash retains its special (escaping) meaning only when followed by $, `, ", \, or newline; command substitution ($(...)) is otherwise performed unconditionally inside double-quoted strings regardless of literal single-quote characters embedded in them -- exactly the mechanism behind the eager-evaluation defect this story fixes.
